input_messages.content: Hello, I’m having trouble sending picture messages from my phone today. I’ve tried a few times, but they just won’t go through. Can you help me fix this?
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I hope that helps!
I’m only using the one phone number, 555-123-2002. That’s the one I’m having trouble with.
I just checked my phone, and I see a little airplane icon at the top. Does that mean something is wrong? I’m not sure if I can make calls or use the internet right now.
Okay, I turned off Airplane Mode like you said. Now I see something that says "No Signal" and "Data Disabled" at the top of my screen. What should I do next?
It looks like my phone is saying there’s no SIM card detected. What does that mean? Is that bad? I haven’t touched anything inside the phone.

Alright, I took out the SIM card and put it back in like you said. Now I see a little signal bar at the top, and it says "2G" and "Data Enabled." Is that good? Can I try sending a picture message now, or is there something else I need to do?
I changed the network setting to prefer 4G and 5G, and now I see "5G" at the top with full signal bars. Should I try sending a picture message now, or is there anything else I need to check first?
I just tried to send a picture message, but it still won’t go through. Is there something else that could be causing this? I thought having 5G would fix it.

I checked my APN settings, and it says the APN name is "internet" and the MMSC URL is "http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc." I’m not sure if that’s right or not. Do I still need to reset anything, or is there something else I should try?

It looks like Wi-Fi Calling is turned on right now. Should I go ahead and turn that off, or do you want me to check the app permissions first? I just want to make sure I’m doing this in the right order.
I turned off Wi-Fi Calling and tried sending a picture message again, but it still won’t go through. This is getting a bit frustrating—why isn’t it working yet? What should I do next?
I checked the permissions for my messaging app, and it has permission for SMS and phone, but I don’t see anything about storage. Could that be the problem? How do I give it permission for storage?

I just gave the messaging app permission to access storage, and now it looks like I can send picture messages again! Thank you so much for your help. Is there anything else I should do to make sure this doesn’t happen again?

Thank you, that’s very helpful advice. I’ll try to remember to check those permissions if I have trouble again. I really appreciate your patience and guidance—it made things a lot less stressful for me!
Thank you so much! I hope you have a wonderful day too. Take care! ###STOP###

user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

Hello, I’m having trouble sending picture messages from my phone today. I’ve tried a few times, but they just won’t go through. Can you help me fix this?

Thank you for reaching out about your issue with sending picture messages (MMS). I can help you troubleshoot this problem.

To get started, I’ll need to identify your account. Could you please provide one of the following:
- The phone number associated with your account,
- Your full name and date of birth,
- Or your customer ID (if you have it)?

Once I have this information, I can begin assisting you further.
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I hope that helps!

Thank you for confirming. I’ve identified your line ending in 2002 and will help you troubleshoot your MMS (picture messaging) issue.

To begin, could you please let me know if you are able to make regular calls and use mobile data (for example, browsing the web) on your phone right now? This will help determine if the issue is specific to MMS or related to your overall service or data connection.
Status Bar: ✈️ Airplane Mode | 🔋 80%
I just checked my phone, and I see a little airplane icon at the top. Does that mean something is wrong? I’m not sure if I can make calls or use the internet right now.

The airplane icon means that Airplane Mode is enabled on your phone. When Airplane Mode is on, all wireless connections—including calls, mobile data, and messaging—are disabled. This is likely the reason you’re unable to send picture messages.

Please turn off Airplane Mode on your phone. You can usually do this by:
1. Swiping down from the top of your screen to open the quick settings menu.
2. Tapping the airplane icon to turn it off.

Once Airplane Mode is off, check if you can send a picture message. Let me know if this resolves the issue or if you need further assistance.

Airplane Mode is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📵 No Signal | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%
Okay, I turned off Airplane Mode like you said. Now I see something that says "No Signal" and "Data Disabled" at the top of my screen. What should I do next?

Thank you for the update. Since you now see "No Signal" and "Data Disabled," it means your phone is not currently connected to the cellular network and mobile data is off. Let’s address these issues step by step:

1. First, let’s check your SIM card status to ensure it’s properly inserted and active.
2. After that, we’ll make sure your mobile data is enabled.

Let’s start by checking your SIM card status. On your phone, please check if there are any messages about the SIM card being missing or locked. If you’re not sure, let me know, and I’ll guide you through the process.
No SIM card detected in the phone.
It looks like my phone is saying there’s no SIM card detected. What does that mean? Is that bad? I haven’t touched anything inside the phone.

If your phone says there’s no SIM card detected, it means your device isn’t able to read the SIM card, which is required for cellular service, calls, texts, and mobile data. This is likely why you’re seeing “No Signal” and can’t send picture messages.

This can sometimes happen even if you haven’t touched the SIM card. It may have shifted slightly or lost contact with the phone’s internal connectors.

Here’s what you should do:
1. Power off your phone.
2. Remove the SIM card tray (usually with a small pin or tool).
3. Take out the SIM card and carefully reinsert it, making sure it’s seated properly.
4. Put the tray back in and power your phone back on.

After you’ve done this, check if your phone now detects the SIM card and if you have signal. Let me know what you see, and we’ll continue troubleshooting if needed.

SIM card re-seated successfully.
Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

Alright, I took out the SIM card and put it back in like you said. Now I see a little signal bar at the top, and it says "2G" and "Data Enabled." Is that good? Can I try sending a picture message now, or is there something else I need to do?

That’s great progress! Your phone now detects the SIM card, and you have a signal with mobile data enabled. However, since it shows "2G," this network type is generally too slow and unreliable for sending picture messages (MMS).

To improve your chances of successfully sending MMS, you should switch your phone’s network mode to prefer 4G or 5G, if available. Please go to your phone’s network settings and select a mode like “4G/5G preferred” or “4G only.”

Once you’ve changed the network mode, wait a moment for your phone to connect to a faster network. Then, try sending a picture message again and let me know if it works or if you need further help.

Preferred Network Mode set to: 4g_5g_preferred
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
I changed the network setting to prefer 4G and 5G, and now I see "5G" at the top with full signal bars. Should I try sending a picture message now, or is there anything else I need to check first?

You’ve done everything correctly so far! With “5G” and full signal bars showing, your phone is now on a fast network and mobile data is enabled. You should be able to send picture messages (MMS) now.

Please try sending a picture message. If it goes through, your issue is resolved. If you still have trouble, let me know, and we can check a few more settings to make sure everything is configured correctly.
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
I just tried to send a picture message, but it still won’t go through. Is there something else that could be causing this? I thought having 5G would fix it.

Thank you for letting me know. Since you’re on 5G with full signal and data enabled, but still can’t send picture messages, the issue could be with your phone’s APN (Access Point Name) settings, which are required for MMS.

The next step is to check your APN settings and reset them if needed. Please check your phone’s APN settings and look for anything unusual, especially the MMSC (Multimedia Messaging Service Center) URL. If you’re not sure how to check this, let me know, and I can guide you through the process.

If you see that the APN or MMSC settings are missing or incorrect, please reset your APN settings to default. After resetting, you’ll need to reboot your phone for the changes to take effect.

Let me know if you need step-by-step instructions for checking or resetting your APN settings.

Current APN Name: internet
MMSC URL (for picture messages): http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc
(These are technical settings, usually best left unchanged.)

I checked my APN settings, and it says the APN name is "internet" and the MMSC URL is "http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc." I’m not sure if that’s right or not. Do I still need to reset anything, or is there something else I should try?

Thank you for checking your APN settings. The APN name and MMSC URL you provided look correct for most carriers, so your APN settings are likely not the issue.

Let’s check a few more things that can affect MMS:
1. Is Wi-Fi Calling enabled on your phone? Sometimes, having Wi-Fi Calling ON can interfere with MMS. If it is enabled, please try turning it OFF and then send a picture message again.
2. Does your messaging app have permission to access storage and SMS? If not, you’ll need to grant those permissions.

Please check if Wi-Fi Calling is enabled and let me know. If you’re unsure how to check, I can guide you through the steps.
Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned ON.

It looks like Wi-Fi Calling is turned on right now. Should I go ahead and turn that off, or do you want me to check the app permissions first? I just want to make sure I’m doing this in the right order.

Please go ahead and turn off Wi-Fi Calling first. After you’ve done that, try sending a picture message again.

If it still doesn’t work, we’ll then check your messaging app’s permissions as the next step. Let me know what happens after you turn off Wi-Fi Calling and try to send the picture message.

Wi-Fi Calling is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
I turned off Wi-Fi Calling and tried sending a picture message again, but it still won’t go through. This is getting a bit frustrating—why isn’t it working yet? What should I do next?

Thank you for your patience. Since turning off Wi-Fi Calling didn’t resolve the issue, the next step is to check your messaging app’s permissions. Sometimes, if the app doesn’t have permission to access storage or SMS, it can’t send or receive picture messages.

Please check your messaging app’s permissions and make sure it has access to:
- Storage (to attach and send pictures)
- SMS (to send messages)

If either of these permissions is missing, please grant them and then try sending a picture message again. Let me know if you need instructions on how to check or change these permissions, or if you’ve already checked and the permissions are correct.
The following apps are installed on the phone: messaging, browser
App 'messaging' has permission for: sms, phone.
I checked the permissions for my messaging app, and it has permission for SMS and phone, but I don’t see anything about storage. Could that be the problem? How do I give it permission for storage?

Yes, not having storage permission can definitely prevent your messaging app from sending picture messages. To fix this, you’ll need to grant storage permission to your messaging app.

Here’s how you can do it:
1. Go to your phone’s Settings.
2. Tap on “Apps” or “Applications.”
3. Find and select your messaging app from the list.
4. Tap on “Permissions.”
5. Look for “Storage” and enable or allow it.

Once you’ve granted storage permission, try sending a picture message again. Let me know if this resolves the issue or if you need further assistance.

Success. Permission 'storage' granted to app 'messaging'.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Your messaging app can send MMS messages.

I just gave the messaging app permission to access storage, and now it looks like I can send picture messages again! Thank you so much for your help. Is there anything else I should do to make sure this doesn’t happen again?

I’m glad to hear that granting storage permission fixed the issue and you can now send picture messages again!

To help prevent this problem in the future:
- Make sure your messaging app always has storage and SMS permissions enabled.
- Avoid disabling these permissions unless necessary.
- If you update your phone or the messaging app, double-check that permissions remain enabled, as updates can sometimes reset them.

If you ever have trouble again, you can follow the same troubleshooting steps or reach out for help. If you have any other questions or need further assistance, feel free to ask!

Thank you, that’s very helpful advice. I’ll try to remember to check those permissions if I have trouble again. I really appreciate your patience and guidance—it made things a lot less stressful for me!

You’re very welcome! I’m glad I could help and make the process easier for you. If you ever need assistance in the future, don’t hesitate to reach out. Have a great day, and enjoy sending your picture messages!
Thank you so much! I hope you have a wonderful day too. Take care! ###STOP###
